hook: Altman turned artificial intelligence from a research field into a consumer phenomenon and a geopolitical agenda item. ChatGPT's November 2022 launch under his leadership put generative AI in hundreds of millions of hands, and his Senate testimony six months later, a CEO asking to be regulated, set the tone for the global governance debate this library documents.
name: Sam Altman

quote.text: If this technology goes wrong, it can go quite wrong.
quote.context: Testimony to the U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee, May 16, 2023

moniker: The Face of the AI Boom

reading.body:
Sam Altman is the single individual most responsible for moving generative AI from a research setting into mass consumer use and into legislative chambers, both shifts documented here by primary sources.

The trajectory the data describes runs in one direction. A nonprofit lab co-founded in 2015 shipped ChatGPT in November 2022, and that product reached an estimated hundred million users in two months. The Senate testimony six months later, in which Altman asked to be regulated rather than resisting oversight, reframed the governance debate in a way that persisted into the policy arguments this library tracks. The November 2023 board crisis, resolved inside five days, is recorded here not as a corporate drama but as evidence that governance-by-charter is structurally fragile when the entity in question controls frontier models.

The data covers Altman's public role and its documented consequences. It does not cover OpenAI's compute infrastructure, its power contracts, or its capital expenditure, so the connection between his leadership decisions and the physical scaling constraints this site treats as binding cannot be drawn from what is here. What the data does establish is that the demand shock ChatGPT created, hundreds of millions of users within weeks of launch, is the proximate reason those infrastructure questions became urgent for the entire industry.
